currentContext.strategies: Evolve from a largely single-category water purifier company into a diversified, multi-category health and hygiene technology company with multiple engines of sustainable, profitable growth|Anchor the transformation on four strategic pillars — strengthening the core water business, expanding the portfolio, delivering service excellence, and building a future-ready D2C company|Strengthen the core water business through innovation, sharper execution and a differentiated omnichannel strategy, with water purifiers remaining the cornerstone and largest driver of value creation|Scale emerging categories — robotic vacuum cleaners, air purifiers and water softeners — which are growing faster than the core and progressively broadening the growth base|Deepen digital and omnichannel capabilities, treating digital capability as an increasingly important competitive advantage|Move from the 'Turnaround' phase to the 'Take-Off' phase: accelerate growth, scale up emerging categories, deepen digital capabilities and strengthen consumer engagement|Pursue a growth agenda centred on four strategic unlocks intended to expand the addressable market, deepen customer engagement and accelerate value creation|Continue targeted investment in innovation, technology and talent, and sustain a culture of customer centricity, agility, collaboration, ownership and accountability|Maintain governance and sustainability as integral to the operating model, with the Board committed to the highest standards of corporate governance, transparency, ethical conduct and risk management|Capital-allocation authority sits with the Board and a dedicated committee structure rather than a stated payout formula in this text. The Board has ultimate responsibility for reviewing and guiding corporate strategy, major plans of action, risk policy, annual budgets and business plans, and for overseeing major capital expenditures, acquisitions and mergers; the Managing Director & CEO and Chief Financial Officer present financials quarterly and management conducts day-long strategy meets with the Board to discuss the operating and capex budget and seek guidance on the Company's future course of action. Alongside five statutory committees (Audit, Nomination & Remuneration, Stakeholders' Relationship, Risk Management and Corporate Social Responsibility), the Company maintains a non-statutory 'Finance Committee' to oversee investments, borrowings and loan approvals, ensuring swift financial decision-making. Related-party transactions are decided by the Audit Committee in strict adherence to applicable laws and governance standards, and the Company maintains a strict policy against political donations.|GC-Mark 'Green Company' certification awarded for both of the Company's manufacturing facilities, alongside a structured approach towards identifying, managing and reducing environmental impacts across operations|BRSR reported on a standalone basis with Limited Assurance obtained from BDO India Services Private Limited|Policies covering all nine NGRBC principles are in place, Board-approved, translated into procedures, and extended to value chain partners, published at the Company's corporate-governance policies page|Data privacy and DPDP Rules implementation programme in place, with customer-data security measures including single sign-on/multi-factor authentication and call masking|Women representation disclosed at 14.3% of the Board of Directors and 33.3% of Key Management Personnel|Grievance redressal mechanisms established for every stakeholder group — communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners — with published web links and multi-channel customer access (call centre, WhatsApp, email, IVR, website, customer app)|Robust human rights, ethics and inclusion framework, with large-scale workforce training and up-skilling as a stated people-risk mitigation|Operations and market reach span 34 national locations (28 States and 6 Union Territories), with exports contributing 0.01% of turnover — an essentially domestic footprint|CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013

risks.risk: Market risk — inability to drive category growth and market share
risks.note: The Company's growth thesis rests on converting very low category penetration into share gains. Mitigations cited include offerings at price points from entry level to premium across products and service, launch of 2X filter life products across the electric water purifier portfolio, significant investment in R&D and marketing capability, an omni-channel go-to-market with access to consumer homes, and targeted action on grey-market operations and consumer education. Financial implication flagged as negative.

risks.risk: Consumer and reputation risk — poor customer experience damaging brand
risks.note: Because the moat is the installed base and after-sales service network, a service failure directly threatens reputation and recurring revenue. Mitigations include fortifying the service network through infrastructure upgrades and expansion, digital capability that gives control to customers, organisational interventions such as 'Customer Day' and deep business-partner engagement, and a revamped incentive model to improve on-slot performance.

risks.risk: Supply chain risk — disruption from geopolitical or other external factors
risks.note: Unexpected supply-chain disruption can constrain product availability. Mitigations include a detailed vendor development roadmap to de-risk the supply network, progressively enhanced strategic partnerships, in-house and domestic manufacturing partnerships in key categories, and strategic up-stocking of inventory given the current geopolitical environment.

Exposure spans cyberattacks, ransomware, data breaches, inadequate disaster recovery and non-compliance with evolving data privacy law such as the DPDP Rules — material for a D2C business holding large volumes of consumer data. Mitigations include a detailed disaster recovery process, data security measures (customer data controls, single sign-on/multi-factor authentication, call masking), organisation-wide cybersecurity awareness training, cyber-security tooling and a DPDP implementation programme.

risks.risk: People risk — people and cultural factors hindering the transformation
risks.note: The transformation agenda depends on leadership depth and execution capability. Mitigations include dedicated teams and capability building for transformation initiatives, large-scale workforce training and up-skilling, employee engagement through continuous leadership connect platforms, a high-performance culture reinforced through rewards and ESOP participation, and a human rights, ethics and inclusion framework.

risks.risk: Product risk — inability to enhance product quality and meet evolving customer needs
risks.note: Quality and relevance drive both first purchase and the service annuity. Mitigations include design improvements such as new flow restrictors and flushing mechanisms with regular review of performance metrics, monitoring for validation of VAVE initiatives and new product development to avoid marketplace quality issues, and a structured approach to identifying, managing and reducing environmental impacts across operations.

risks.risk: Input cost inflation and currency depreciation
risks.note: The MD&A notes inflationary pressures strengthened toward the end of FY26 as higher crude oil prices and currency depreciation increased input and consumer costs, with inflation expected to rise before moderating — a direct margin and pricing risk for a consumer durables manufacturer.

The cautionary statement flags that actual results may differ materially, with demand and supply conditions, changes in government regulations, exchange rates, tax laws, monsoons, natural hazards, and national and global economic developments identified as factors that could influence operations. Category-level constraints cited include low penetration, consumer price sensitivity and limited awareness in certain markets.

one-line thesis: Eureka Forbes delivered strong Q4FY26 with 11.6% revenue growth and record 13.2% EBITDA margins, successfully transitioning from a single-category player to a multi-category health brand while navigating input cost inflation via a 6-7% price hike. The strategic pivot toward high-margin recurring revenue (filters, multi-year AMCs) and localization of robotics manufacturing underpins the FY27 guidance of holding margins despite macro headwinds.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 684cr (+11.6% YoY); Full Year: INR 2,710cr (+11.3% YoY). EBITDA: INR 90cr (+13.1% YoY), Margin 13.2% (record high); Full Year Margin 12.2% (+55bps). PAT: INR 51cr (Q4), INR 160cr Reported FY26 (incl. Wage Code one-off in Q3), INR 190cr Normalized/Pre-exceptional (+19% YoY). Order Book: Not applicable (B2C model); Deferred Income Liability (AMC base) grew 9% aggregate with shift to non-current (multi-year). Net Debt: Net Cash surplus of INR 443cr (improved from INR 193cr net debt in Jun-22). One-offs: Wage Code impact absorbed in Q3 FY26; Input cost inflation (West Asia crisis, currency) mitigated by April price hike.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Double-digit growth targeted for product business; Service revenue expected to step up to double-digits as filter initiatives mature. Margins: Aim to 'at least hold' FY26 levels (12.2%+) despite input cost pressures. Order Inflow: Sustained double-digit AMC bookings growth continuing into FY27. Capex/Commissioning: Localization of robotics assembly with Dixon starting next 3-4 months; BIS QCO compliance by Sep-2026.
order book & pipeline: N/A for B2C; Key metric is Deferred Income Liability which grew 9% YoY, with significant mix shift to non-current liabilities indicating higher multi-year AMC penetration locking in future revenue.
segment / subsidiary detail: Water Purifiers: Double-digit growth, 3-year CAGR >12%. Robotics: >65% share of vacuum category, on track for INR 1,000cr revenue by FY30. Air Purifiers: Grew 2.7x in FY26 (low base). Water Softeners: Strong double-digit growth. Filters: New growth vector launched in Q3/Q4 with simplified assortment and influencer campaigns (1B+ views).
growth verticals / optionality: Unlocking the installed base for genuine filter replacements (currently leaking to gray market); Expansion of robotics into organized retail and super-premium segments; Geographic expansion of air purifiers beyond North India; Potential service platformization for third-party categories long-term.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin: 58.8% FY26 (+46bps); under pressure in FY27 from polymer/metal costs and currency. Mitigation: 6-7% price increase implemented in April FY27; aggressive COGS program and efficiency drives to remove leakages. Operating Leverage: Employee cost % dropped to 12.1% from 12.6%.
capex / expansion: FY26 Capex: INR 84cr (up from INR 55cr in FY25). Focus on manufacturing localization (SKD assembly with Dixon) and digital service infrastructure. No major greenfield capacity expansion mentioned; asset-light assembly model for robotics.
capital allocation: Balance sheet strengthened to Net Cash INR 443cr; Free Cash Flow INR 237cr (148% of reported PAT). Capital allocated to growth investments (A&SP up 13.2%) and inorganic M&A opportunities identified as strategic priority given cash surplus.
risks & watch-items: Sustained input cost inflation exceeding pricing actions; Consumer demand softening due to inflation/drought concerns (management sees low risk); Disruption from quick-commerce/service aggregators (Urban Company) in after-sales space; Execution risk in changing consumer behavior for filter purchases.
management quality / tone: Confident and resilient; Acknowledges macro uncertainty (geopolitics, costs) but emphasizes strong fundamentals, record margins, and successful category diversification. Tone is proactive on pricing and defensive on cost efficiency.
non-obvious takeaways: Shift in AMC accounting mix: Aggressive push for multi-year contracts has moved significant deferred revenue from 'current' to 'non-current' liabilities, potentially masking the immediate top-line velocity of new bookings while securing long-term visibility. Service disruption pilots: Exploring 4-hour service turnaround models analogous to quick-commerce, currently in pilot phase.

themes.title: Consumer durables, cooling & electricals
themes.need: Rising incomes, electrification and a record cooling season drive consumer-electricals and appliances - HAVELLS/VOLTAS/BLUESTARCO/SYMPHONY/ORIENTELEC on cooling & electricals; TTKPRESTIG/STOVEKRAFT/BAJAJELEC/EUREKAFORB on kitchen/home; CROMPTON-tier fans & pumps; premiumization + GST 2.0 + summer demand expand the organized share. Q1FY27's small-cap read: SONAMLTD grew revenue 75.6% YoY to INR 66.57cr on a cheap raw-material inventory position taken 6-7 months in advance while selling prices rose - management explicitly called the 75% print non-repeatable and guided FY27 to 25-30% with a Q2 floor of INR 40-50cr - and is pivoting from volume to INR 5,000-15,000 value clocks with capacity utilisation still only 60-70%.

hero.oneLiner: Eureka Forbes is one of India's leading consumer health and hygiene companies, built around the Aquaguard water purifier franchise and one of the largest after-sales service networks in Indian consumer durables, now transforming into a diversified, D2C-led health and hygiene solutions provider.
hero.industry: Consumer Durables / Home Health & Hygiene Solutions

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Eureka Forbes is one of India's leading consumer health and hygiene companies, built around the Aquaguard water purifier franchise and one of the largest after-sales service networks in Indian consumer durables, now transforming into a diversified, D2C-led health and hygiene solutions provider.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Eureka Forbes Limited, with a legacy spanning over four decades, sells health and hygiene products and services to Indian households and institutions through its flagship Aquaguard brand and allied portfolio. Its offering spans water purifiers, vacuum cleaners (including robotic vacuum cleaners), air purifiers, water softeners and services including aftermarket filters and annual maintenance contracts. The Company was an early adopter of the direct-to-consumer model in India and reaches customers through an integrated multi-channel approach of direct sales, retail (modern and general trade) and e-commerce, supported by an extensive service infrastructure.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Forbes Aquatech Limited — subsidiary: Subsidiary (CIN: U28122KA2003PLC032492) incorporated 03 September 2003 to manufacture, trade in and distribute water filters, water purifiers and allied products, and to execute works relating to water purification; the Company holds unquoted equity shares in it.
- Infinite Water Solutions Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly Owned Subsidiary (CIN: U74999MH2008PTC180918) incorporated 07 April 2008 for water filters, purifiers and water purification systems, including manufacture and processing of home reverse osmosis membrane elements and related water treatment products; the Company holds unquoted equity shares in it.
- Euro Forbes Limited — subsidiary: Wholly Owned Subsidiary (registration number 145214) incorporated 12 April 2011 in Dubai for general trading and investment holding worldwide, including investment in overseas entities and Jebel Ali Free Zone approved projects; the equity investment carried in the Company's books is fully impaired, the impairment having arisen in the books of the demerged undertaking merged into the Company with effect from 01 February 2022.
- Forbes Lux FZE, Dubai — subsidiary: Referred to in the Board's Report as having been liquidated during the year under review.
- Water Quality Association — related party: Non-profit organisation in which the Company holds a small unquoted equity investment classified under 'Investments in Equity Instruments - Other Company'; fair value considered the same as carrying value given its non-profit nature.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Water Purifiers: Double-digit growth, 3-year CAGR >12%. Robotics: >65% share of vacuum category, on track for INR 1,000cr revenue by FY30. Air Purifiers: Grew 2.7x in FY26 (low base). Water Softeners: Strong double-digit growth. Filters: New growth vector launched in Q3/Q4 with simplified assortment and influencer campaigns (1B+ views).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Electric Water Purifiers:** Aquaguard
- **Vacuum Cleaners:** Vacuum cleaners, Robotic vacuum cleaners
- **Air Purifiers:** Air purifiers
- **Water Softeners:** Water softeners
- **Service:** After-sales service, Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMC), Aftermarket filters

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India — domestic consumer health and hygiene market
- Urban households, with adoption expanding beyond metropolitan markets into Tier-2, Tier-3 and emerging urban centres
- Commercial establishments, healthcare facilities and educational institutions (air purification)
- B2B (included within the 'Others' category alongside air purifiers and softeners)

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: N/A for B2C; Key metric is Deferred Income Liability which grew 9% YoY, with significant mix shift to non-current liabilities indicating higher multi-year AMC penetration locking in future revenue.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Double-digit growth targeted for product business; Service revenue expected to step up to double-digits as filter initiatives mature. Margins: Aim to 'at least hold' FY26 levels (12.2%+) despite input cost pressures. Order Inflow: Sustained double-digit AMC bookings growth continuing into FY27. Capex/Commissioning: Localization of robotics assembly with Dixon starting next 3-4 months; BIS QCO compliance by Sep-2026.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Unlocking the installed base for genuine filter replacements (currently leaking to gray market); Expansion of robotics into organized retail and super-premium segments; Geographic expansion of air purifiers beyond North India; Potential service platformization for third-party categories long-term.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The Company's categories are aligned with India's strongest long-term consumption themes — health, hygiene, wellness and convenience — with demand supported by rising incomes, rapid urbanisation, growing health awareness and an expanding middle class
- Category penetration across water purifiers, robotic cleaning, air purifiers and water softeners remains extremely low versus global benchmarks, leaving a long runway for growth
- Structural shifts — higher female workforce participation, dual-income households, improved household infrastructure and preference for organised service providers — are driving demand for both products and after-sales service, creating recurring service opportunities across the installed base
- Water purifier category growth accelerated from low single digits in the pre-transformation period, driven by stronger innovation, sharper execution and a differentiated omnichannel strategy; offline retail delivered robust growth while online tertiary sales stayed healthy
- Emerging categories (robotic vacuum cleaners, air purifiers, water softeners) are growing at an even faster pace than the core, diversifying the growth base and reducing single-category dependence
- Premiumisation and the shift from traditional to robotic/smart vacuum cleaners is a mix driver, with AI-enabled features, smart navigation and app controls accelerating adoption
- Management expects the Indian water purifier industry to deliver high-single-digit to low-double-digit growth in both volume and value through the remainder of the decade, supported by water-quality concerns, expanding piped-water access and rising household incomes
- Government-led initiatives to improve access to piped water are expanding the addressable market, particularly in rural India, while consumer preference for premium technology-enabled products supports value growth
- Macro headwinds flagged: geopolitical tensions including the West Asia crisis, rising commodity inflation and currency depreciation raising input costs, and evolving consumer spending patterns
- India's medium-term growth outlook remains favourable, with the IMF projecting GDP growth of 6.5% in FY27, supporting resilient domestic consumption

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross Margin: 58.8% FY26 (+46bps); under pressure in FY27 from polymer/metal costs and currency. Mitigation: 6-7% price increase implemented in April FY27; aggressive COGS program and efficiency drives to remove leakages. Operating Leverage: Employee cost % dropped to 12.1% from 12.6%.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Balance sheet strengthened to Net Cash INR 443cr; Free Cash Flow INR 237cr (148% of reported PAT). Capital allocated to growth investments (A&SP up 13.2%) and inorganic M&A opportunities identified as strategic priority given cash surplus.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed annual-report text discloses no named plant, capacity or capex project with a commissioning, completion or ramp timeline. Expansion at Eureka Forbes is described in capability and category terms rather than capacity terms: the Board's Report states that the transformation initiatives undertaken by the Company are aimed at strengthening its core water business, expanding its presence in adjacent health and hygiene categories such as robotic vacuum cleaning, enhancing direct-to-consumer and omni-channel capabilities, and leveraging digital technologies to improve customer experience and operational effectiveness. Alongside this, the Company says it continued to invest in product innovation, brand building, talent development and capability enhancement to support its long-term growth aspirations. The addressable-market expansion the Company points to is industry-led — the MD&A cites Technopak/management estimates for water purifier product and service, water softeners, vacuum cleaners and air purifiers growing to a materially larger market by FY30 off very low penetration — but no company-specific capacity addition, greenfield site or project timeline is stated in this text.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and resilient; Acknowledges macro uncertainty (geopolitics, costs) but emphasizes strong fundamentals, record margins, and successful category diversification. Tone is proactive on pricing and defensive on cost efficiency.

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": false, "note": "The Board's Report states that no significant and material orders were passed by regulators, courts or tribunals impacting the going concern status and the Company's future operations, and that there were no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position between the year end and the date of the report.", "as_of": "2026-07-25"}

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Flagship Aquaguard brand with strong market presence and a trusted reputation among Indian consumers; historically the market leader in water purifiers
- One of the largest after-sales service networks in the Indian consumer durables industry, supporting customer retention, recurring revenue and brand loyalty
- Early adopter of the direct-to-consumer model in India, giving long-standing customer relationships through its sales and service network
- Integrated multi-channel distribution — direct sales, retail (modern and general trade) and e-commerce — enabling wide market coverage
- Diversified health and hygiene portfolio across water purifiers, vacuum cleaners, air purifiers, water softeners and services, reducing dependence on any single category
- Recurring revenue streams from services, AMC and filters, with AMC bookings growing double-digit in every quarter of FY26
- Significant investment in innovation, premiumisation, affordability, digital capabilities, operational excellence and talent over the transformation period

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Sustained input cost inflation exceeding pricing actions; Consumer demand softening due to inflation/drought concerns (management sees low risk); Disruption from quick-commerce/service aggregators (Urban Company) in after-sales space; Execution risk in changing consumer behavior for filter purchases.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Shift in AMC accounting mix: Aggressive push for multi-year contracts has moved significant deferred revenue from 'current' to 'non-current' liabilities, potentially masking the immediate top-line velocity of new bookings while securing long-term visibility. Service disruption pilots: Exploring 4-hour service turnaround models analogous to quick-commerce, currently in pilot phase.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Evolve from a largely single-category water purifier company into a diversified, multi-category health and hygiene technology company with multiple engines of sustainable, profitable growth
- Anchor the transformation on four strategic pillars — strengthening the core water business, expanding the portfolio, delivering service excellence, and building a future-ready D2C company
- Strengthen the core water business through innovation, sharper execution and a differentiated omnichannel strategy, with water purifiers remaining the cornerstone and largest driver of value creation
- Scale emerging …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Input cost inflation (polymers/metals) and currency depreciation pressuring COGS | Dixon Technologies | beneficiary | Med | Eureka Forbes is migrating robotics manufacturing from imported finished goods to SKD assembly with Dixon to comply with BIS QCO by Sep-2026, potentially increasing Dixon's order book. |
| Service aggregation platforms threatening traditional OEM service monopolies | Urban Company | loser | Low | While Urban Company disrupts general home services, Eureka Forbes is doubling down on proprietary tech and multi-year locks to retain sticky high-value appliance servicing, limiting immediate share loss. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Exceptional item] "Reported PAT includes one-time pre-tax gain of Rs. 19.5 Cr due to reversal of gratuity expense" — a non-recurring item flagged in three separate footnotes.
- [Category runway] A Technopak whitepaper plus management estimates table titled "Under Penetrated Categories With Long Runway For Growth" sizes the combined opportunity at Rs. 9,749 Cr in FY23 growing to Rs. 26,300 Cr by FY30E at a 15% CAGR, with per-category penetration shown as Water Purifier–Product 7%, Water Purifier–Service <25%, Water Softeners <1%, Vacuum Cleaners 2%, Air Purifiers 1%.
- [Macro drivers] Supportive macro cited as urbanisation ("By 2036, 40% of Indians will live in towns and cities, up from 31% in 2011"), a middle class reaching "1 Billion by 2047", female labour force participation "increased from 33% in 2022 to 42% in 2024", piped water households "up from 16.8% in 2019 to 77.2% Households in 2024", and electricity access at "99.5%" of population in 2023.
- [Leadership] A nine-member management team is profiled under MD & CEO Pratik Pota (33+ years, ex-Jubilant FoodWorks, PepsiCo, Airtel, HUL), including CFO Gaurav Khandelwal, Chief Growth Officer Anurag Kumar and CTO–R&D and Manufacturing Suresh Redhu.
- [Outlook language] Management states "while the external environment remains uncertain, the fundamentals of our business remain strong" and that the company is "focused on stepping up growth and unlocking the next phase of our transformation journey".
